summary: Yukihiko Matsumura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Matsumura studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and served there as a specialist researcher (attested 2026).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Yukihiro Okada studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn. Okada held posts at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College and Minobusan University.
Yukihisa Yamao (1935–2021) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from around 1954 to 1964 and later held a post there from around 1970 to 2006.
Yukio Hattori (1932–2007) worked in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University and held an academic post at Japan Women's University.

Yukio Kotani (born 1931) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Having studied under Hanjiro Tominaga, Kotani held a post as professor emeritus of comparative literature at Rissho University from around 1970 to 2002.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tohoku University. He was a professor at Toyo University and served as professor and president at Rissho University.

Yukio Takeda (1934–2021) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1963). He held posts at Nagoya City University, Hokkaido University, the University of Tokyo (~1978–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University.

Yukio Yamanaka specializes in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Yamanaka studied at Kyoto University and the University of Freiburg, holding posts at the University of Göttingen and Ryukoku University's Research Center for World Buddhist Culture.

Yuko Kamishima (born 1971) specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Indiana University Bloomington, the University of Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at Waseda University and Ritsumeikan University.
Yuko Matsuda works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Matsuda studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held an academic post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. Yokochi has served as an associate professor at Kyoto University.
Yulian Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at Fo Guang University. Zeng studied under Kirill Solonin and traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Katayama pursued PhD studies at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) under the supervision of Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).
Yumi Nakamoto works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Nakamoto studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2014) and also held a research post there in 2012.
Yumiko Ishihama (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from around 1981 to 1993 and held a post there around 1996.

Yumin Dai works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Dai studied at Hebei University, Nanjing University, and the University of Arizona, becoming an assistant professor at Nanjing University in 2019.

Yumzhana Zhabon works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Zhabon studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1979–1985) and became a senior researcher at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies in 1985.
Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at Fudan University by 2006. Ji served as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

Yung-Jong Shiah works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. After completing a PhD at the University of Edinburgh (2003–2008), Shiah became Chair Professor and Dean of the College of Buddhist Studies at Fo Guang University in 2025.
Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ma completed a PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).
